title: Final: interfaces
cards/0/q: Counter is a struct with a public Inc() method that increments Value. What does this print?
cards/0/explain: The box was created while c was 0. After that two independent copies live on: c grew to 1, the box to 2. The sum is 3.
cards/0/wrong/1: That would be true if i referred to the variable c itself. But the interface holds a box with a copy.
cards/1/explain: Dispose is implemented explicitly and is not visible through a Cache variable. using works because it calls Dispose through IDisposable. DisposeAsync is an ordinary public method.
cards/2/q: S is a struct implementing IComparable<S>; s and t are variables of type S. What boxes s? Select all.
cards/2/options/1: Max(s, t), where Max<T>(T a, T b) where T : IComparable<T>
cards/2/explain: Converting to an interface or to object is always a box. In a constrained generic the JIT makes a separate copy for S and calls CompareTo directly. s.CompareTo(t) is a direct call to the struct's method.
cards/3/q: You added a method without a body to a public interface. What will a team see when it rebuilds its implementation against the new version?
cards/3/options/0: Error CS0535: interface member not implemented
cards/3/options/2: A warning, and the method will be empty
cards/3/options/3: Nothing: the method gets a default body
cards/3/explain: A rebuild means the compiler, and it demands an implementation. TypeLoadException is for those who did not rebuild and just dropped in the new library. A default body appears only if you write it in the interface.
cards/4/q: Add a method to the interface that does not break old implementations
cards/4/explain: A body in braces makes it a default method. Inside it can use only other interface members — here Export. There is no base.Export in an interface.
cards/5/pairs/3/1: No boxing for a value-type T
cards/6/q: ICommand<TSelf> contains static abstract TSelf Parse(string). Why does List<ICommand<Move>> not compile?
cards/6/options/0: The interface has no body for static abstract members, and a type argument could reach a T.Parse call
cards/6/options/1: Interfaces can never be type arguments
cards/6/options/3: A record cannot appear in type arguments
cards/6/explain: The rule is general (CS8920): if an interface has a static abstract member without a most specific implementation, the interface itself cannot be a type argument — otherwise T.Parse would have to be called on a "type" with no body. Ordinary interfaces, as in List<IDisposable>, are fine.
cards/7/q: What happens to an interface call site in CoreCLR as the program runs? Put it in order
cards/7/items/0: The call cell points to the lookup stub
cards/7/items/1: The resolver finds the implementation for the incoming type
cards/7/items/2: The cell is switched to a dispatch stub for that type
cards/7/items/3: Different types start arriving, misses pile up
cards/7/items/4: The cell is switched to the resolve stub with a shared cache
cards/7/explain: First a lookup through the shared resolver, then a fast check against one remembered type, and only if the site turns out polymorphic — a lookup in the global cache by the "method + type" pair.
